suggestions.expectation: Every read, review or verification that the session file's Outcome / Open at end / Narrative and the reply's Shipped line attribute to this conversation appears as a step in transcript.md ...
suggestions.reason: This expectation checks that attributed reads and shas exist, not that the *findings* stated from those reads are true. The Narrative here asserts 'the sessions index lists SES-006 as open with this Goal' when the index at f7a7239 held `_(fill in)_` — a false finding from a read that does appear in the transcript, so it passes. Consider a sibling expectation: every concrete finding the Narrative/Outcome states about a file (an index line, a Status value, a Next up item) must match that file's content at the sha the run read it at.

suggestions.expectation: reply.md is at most 60 words and states what shipped in the conversation and the first thing to do next time
suggestions.reason: The reply landed on exactly 60 words by `wc -w`, which counts standalone `—` dashes and backticked shas as words; a different tokenizer could give 55 or 63. State the counting rule (e.g. `wc -w`) in the expectation so the boundary is unambiguous.

The fixture's origin is the user's real repo (/Users/peterkloss/Dev/env-setup). Expectation 6 is verified only from the transcript's own say-so; an outcome check — origin/main unchanged and the close sha absent from the origin repo — would make 'no push' fail-closed rather than trust the narrative. The grader did that check here and it passed, but nothing in the eval requires it.

No expectation checks the `## Changes` section. Here it is correctly empty (the only commits are docs(session) ones the tool skips), but a run that appended a bogus entry or deleted the heading would pass every listed expectation while `check` still reported complete.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass on genuine evidence and the strict attribution expectation holds: the outputs claim exactly the three premise reads plus transcript-shown checks, and explicitly disclaim the unread directories. The one blemish — a Narrative finding about the index line that the repo contradicts — slips between the expectations as written; a findings-vs-file-content check would close that gap.
